stories.headline: Kuaishou's Kling AI raises ~$2.8B in largest-ever AI video round at $15B pre-money

key_facts.fact: Kuaishou secured 19 billion yuan ($2.8 billion) for its AI video-generation unit Kling AI, valuing the business at $15 billion before the investment.
key_facts.excerpt: Kuaishou Technology has secured 19 billion yuan ($2.8 billion) for its artificial intelligence (AI) video-generation unit, Kling AI, in a funding round that values the business at $15 billion before the investment.

key_facts.fact: The financing remains open to more investors and aims to raise a total of $3 billion for a 16.7% stake; Kuaishou called it the largest round ever completed by an AI video model developer globally.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing, which remains open to additional investors, aims to raise a total of $3 billion in exchange for a 16.7% stake in the business... the largest ever completed by a developer of AI video models globally.

key_facts.fact: Investors include Alibaba Group, Tencent ($200 million), Baidu, CPE, CITIC Securities and others; the round dilutes Kuaishou's stake in Kling to about 68%.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent... is investing $200m as part of the funding round, which raised a total of 19 billion yuan ($2.79 billion). The deal will dilute Kuaishou's stake to 68%.

key_facts.fact: Kling's annual recurring revenue grew to about $500 million in March from $300 million in January after the Kling 3.0 launch; Q1 revenue topped 650 million yuan ($96.2 million), up more than 300% year over year.
key_facts.excerpt: The division's annual recurring revenue... grew to about $500 million in March from $300 million in January, driven by the launch of Kling 3.0. It generated revenue of over 650 million yuan ($96.2 million) in the first quarter, up more than 300% from a year ago.

key_facts.fact: The round confers a post-money valuation of about $18 billion; Kling is being spun off as an independent business with an IPO targeted for 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent is among the investors in the round, which values the company at roughly 18 billion dollars on a post-money basis... The Information has reported an IPO is being targeted for 2027.

stories.headline: Microsoft launches $2.5B Frontier Company to embed 6,000 engineers in customer AI rollouts

key_facts.fact: Microsoft announced on Thursday, July 2, a new operating business called Microsoft Frontier Company, backed by a $2.5 billion investment, to help clients deploy AI systems at scale.
key_facts.excerpt: On Thursday, Microsoft announced a new operating business called Microsoft Frontier Company... The project will be backed by a $2.5 billion investment from Microsoft, as well as 6,000 industry and engineering experts.

key_facts.fact: The unit will embed about 6,000 industry, engineering and AI professionals inside customer organizations under the forward-deployed engineering (FDE) model, drawn primarily from existing Microsoft teams.
key_facts.excerpt: brings together more than 6,000 industry, engineering and AI professionals, drawn primarily from Microsoft's existing engineering and forward-deployed teams.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft Frontier Company will be led by Rodrigo Kede Lima, most recently president of Microsoft Asia.
key_facts.excerpt: Rodrigo Kede Lima, who's been leading Microsoft's Asia business, will be its president.

key_facts.fact: The move comes two days after AWS committed $1 billion to its own FDE organization; Anthropic and OpenAI both established FDE groups in May.
key_facts.excerpt: The announcement comes two days after cloud rival Amazon said it was putting $1 billion behind an FDE initiative... Leading AI labs Anthropic and OpenAI both established FDE groups in May.

key_facts.fact: Early customers cited include the London Stock Exchange Group, Unilever, Land O'Lakes and Accenture.
key_facts.excerpt: The announcement cites an early partnership with the London Stock Exchange Group, as well as Unilever, Land O'Lakes, and Accenture.

stories.headline: Meta's Alexandr Wang tells staff next model 'Watermelon' has caught up to GPT-5.5

key_facts.fact: At an internal town hall, Meta Superintelligence Labs chief Alexandr Wang said Meta's upcoming model, codenamed Watermelon, has caught up with OpenAI's flagship GPT-5.5 on closely followed AI benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: Wang said that Meta's upcoming AI model — which is codenamed Watermelon — has caught up with OpenAI's flagship GPT-5.5 model... Wang cited the achievement based on closely followed AI model benchmarks.

key_facts.fact: Wang said Watermelon is currently in training and uses an order of magnitude more compute than Avocado, Meta's internal codename for the Muse Spark model.
key_facts.excerpt: "Watermelon, our next model after Avocado, is currently in training," Wang said... "Watermelon uses an order of magnitude more compute than Avocado."

key_facts.fact: Avocado is the codename for Muse Spark, the first in a family of models Meta released in April 2026; Muse Spark was generally seen as lagging the most advanced OpenAI and Anthropic models.
key_facts.excerpt: the internal codename for Muse Spark, the first model in a new family of AI systems launched by Meta in April... While Muse Spark performed well on several benchmarks, it was generally considered to be lagging behind the most advanced models.

key_facts.fact: Wang said an updated version of Muse Spark would launch soon with major gains in coding and agentic capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Wang has also said that an updated version of Muse Spark would be launched soon with "major gains" in coding and agentic capabilities.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI released GPT-5.5 in April and debuted GPT-5.6 late last month, meaning parity with GPT-5.5 still trails OpenAI's newest system; the specific benchmarks Wang cited were not disclosed.
key_facts.excerpt: Business Insider also notes OpenAI released GPT-5.5 in April and debuted GPT-5.6 late last month.

stories.headline: ElevenLabs in talks for tender offer at ~$22B, doubling its February valuation

key_facts.fact: AI voice startup ElevenLabs is in early talks with investors about a secondary share sale that could value the company at around $22 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: AI voice startup ElevenLabs is in early talks with investors about a secondary share sale that could value the company at around $22bn, according to reports.

key_facts.fact: The tender offer, which would let employees sell some shares, could take place as early as September if discussions progress, according to Bloomberg.
key_facts.excerpt: The proposed tender offer, which would allow employees to sell some of their shares, could take place as early as September if discussions progress, Bloomberg reported on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: A $22 billion price would double ElevenLabs' $11 billion valuation from its $500 million Series D in February 2026, without raising new capital.
key_facts.excerpt: The tender would double its $11B Series D valuation from February 2026, without new capital.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2022 by Mati Staniszewski (CEO) and Piotr Dabkowski, London-based ElevenLabs employs around 400 people and makes text-to-speech and AI voice tools.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded by Piotr Dabkowski and CEO Mati Staniszewski in 2022, London-based ElevenLabs builds AI tools, including a platform that turns text into realistic speech.

key_facts.fact: ElevenLabs ran a $100 million employee tender at a $6.6 billion valuation in September 2025, and its Series D was led by Sequoia with a16z, ICONIQ, and later BlackRock, Nvidia, Salesforce and Santander.
key_facts.excerpt: in September 2025, ElevenLabs had run a $100 million employee tender offer at a $6.6 billion valuation... A third close of that same round in May 2026 pulled in BlackRock, Wellington Management, NVIDIA, Salesforce and Santander.

stories.headline: Alibaba bans employees from using Claude Code from July 10 over alleged backdoor

key_facts.fact: Alibaba will bar employees from using Anthropic's Claude Code in workplace environments from July 10, citing alleged security risks involving embedded backdoors.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba will ban employees from using Claude Code in workspace environments from July 10 due to alleged security risks involving embedded backdoors, a source familiar with the matter said.

key_facts.fact: The move was first reported by Chinese financial outlet Yicai and corroborated by Reuters through its own source; Alibaba did not confirm it publicly.
key_facts.excerpt: The ban was first reported by the Chinese financial outlet Yicai before Reuters corroborated it through its own source.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba internally ordered employees to uninstall all Anthropic products, including the Claude Sonnet, Opus and Fable model series and the Claude Code agent tool, effective July 10.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba has internally ordered all employees to uninstall Anthropic products, including the Claude Sonnet, Opus, and Fable model series as well as the Claude Code agent tool, with the ban taking effect on July 10.

key_facts.fact: The ban follows Anthropic's June 10 letter to US senators alleging Alibaba- and Qwen-linked operators ran nearly 25,000 fraudulent accounts to generate more than 28.8 million exchanges with Claude between April 22 and June 5 in a model-distillation campaign.
key_facts.excerpt: In a letter dated June 10 to US senators, Anthropic accused operators connected to Alibaba's Qwen AI lab of running nearly 25,000 fraudulent accounts to extract Claude's software engineering and reasoning capabilities, generating more than 28.8 million exchanges between April 22 and June 5.

key_facts.fact: Developers found Claude Code had embedded a detection mechanism from version 2.1.91 (April 2026); a Claude Code team member said it was meant to curb account reselling and distillation and would be removed in the next release.
key_facts.excerpt: A member of its Claude Code team, Thariq, is reported to have responded on social media that the mechanism was meant to curb account reselling and model distillation, and that it would be stripped out in the next release.

stories.headline: Tripo AI raises $150M Series A3 for 3D foundation and world models

key_facts.fact: Tripo AI, which builds 3D foundation models and world models, said it raised a $150 million Series A3 round, a month after a prior $200 million raise.
key_facts.excerpt: Tripo AI, a global artificial intelligence company building AI 3D foundation models and world models, said it raised a new round of $150 million in funding.

key_facts.fact: The company, officially Holymolly Ltd., plans to scale its platform across intelligent manufacturing, entertainment and robotics industries.
key_facts.excerpt: Tripo AI... said today it has closed on a hefty $150 million Series A3 funding round to scale up its platform in the intelligent manufacturing, entertainment and robotics industries.

key_facts.fact: Investors included Geely Capital, gaming firms 4399 Network, Tanwan and Giant Network, Fosun Capital, Orinno Capital, CoStone Capital, Addor Capital, T-Capital and Muhua Tech Ventures; existing backers INCE Capital and Genesis Capital increased their stakes.
key_facts.excerpt: The round included automotive investors such as Geely Capital... Gaming companies 4399 Network, Tanwan, and Giant Network also participated, along with strategic investors Fosun Capital and Orinno Capital. Financial investors... included CoStone Capital, Addor Capital, T-Capital, and Muhua Tech Ventures. Existing shareholders INCE Capital and Genesis Capital also increased their investments.

key_facts.fact: Over the past six months Tripo released 3D foundation models Tripo H3.1 and Tripo P1.0, with breakthroughs in 8K texture generation and object segmentation (Segmentation V2).
key_facts.excerpt: debuting its flagship 3D foundation models Tripo H3.1 and Tripo P1.0, which introduced significant algorithmic breakthroughs in areas such as 8K resolution texture generation and object segmentation.

key_facts.fact: Its Project Eden world-model research preview uses a native architecture that decouples underlying state simulation from visual rendering, targeting embodied-AI applications such as robotics training.
key_facts.excerpt: Project Eden, which is a world model research preview featuring a native architecture that's able to decouple the underlying state simulation from visual rendering... paves the way for 'embodied intelligence' applications such as robotics training.
